"The house has an advantage in blackjack simply because the player has to draw first and if he busts, the player automatically losses regardless if the dealer subsequently busts in the same round. This is the casino's solitary advantage in blackjack and if everything were equal, the house edge in blackjack would be about 8 percent."

From: http://www.blackjackbee.com/blackjack_odds.php

Hey guys,

I rarely drink sweetened coffee, but when I do it's normally a special treat like Starbucks. Day before yesterday I had a Mini-Chai Creme frappuccino (coconut milk, no whip: 117 cal), while I was out and about.

Then, yesterday thinking a coffee frappuccino would stave off hunger even better than a tea frappuccino, I had a mini, coconut, no whip coffee frappuccino (138 calories), but I wound up regretting the waste of calories when I felt hungry later in the day.

So, today, instead of Starbucks, I had a cup of Folgers French Vanilla coffee, with 1/2 cup unsweetened cashew milk, and 2 teaspoons turbinado sugar. 43 calories. Higher volume and more satisfying than a Starbucks drink with three times the calories. I think sweetened coffee keeps me feeling more satiated and for longer, than unsweetened coffee, and it really only takes a little sugar.

Here I was, worrying about which were the lowest calories Starbucks drinks, when really, if I was willing to spend 117+ calories on coffee, I should have just thought of having sweetened coffee at home. I guess it seems obvious, but since I almost have like a hard and fast rule about never sweetening my coffee, and I think of Starbucks in the meal/snack/splurge category, it just didn't cross my mind.

Sometimes the solution is really so simple it's right under your nose.
